text.p: Englishman Ronnie O'Sullivan, who made a maximum 147 in the first round, snatched the last two frames to take a 9-7 lead over Darren Morgan in the second round of the world championship on Friday.
The 21-year-old eighth seed stayed on course for a quarter-final against titleholder Stephen Hendry, who battled back from 4-1 down to draw level with Mark Williams in their second round encounter.
O'Sullivan was fortunate to lead Morgan, a dour Welshman who had chances in the last two frames and who can count himself unlucky to be trailing.
The exciting Englishman needs to win just four more frames when the best-of-25-frame match resumes on Saturday morning to set up the possible clash with Hendry.
The Scot did well to stay with Williams, the Welshman who whipped him 9-2 in the British Open final this month - Hendry's worst loss in a final.
Williams, a superb potter, had chances to move further ahead as Hendry made unaccustomed errors but could not capitalise.
In another second round match, Canadian 14th seed Alain Robidoux lead 5-3 against England's Stefan Mazrocis, who upset third seed Peter Ebdon in the first round.
